newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Most rail basis offers fall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Most rail basis offers fall.

text.p: Most basis offers for soymeal by rail were lower Monday in response to heavy supplies of soymeal, soymeal dealers said.
"We had a big crush on hand last week, and we'll have another big one on hand this week," said a southeast U.S. dealer.
Heavy losses in CBOT soymeal futures caused most end-users to stay out of the spot market Monday, dealers said.
At 1018 CDT, July soymeal futures were $6.50 per ton lower at $255.70, and other months were $5.80 to $10.00 per ton lower.

CBOT futures were sharply lower on forecasts showing much higher-than-expected 1997/98 (Aug/Sep) soybean acreage. The U.S. Department of Agriculture put soybean acreage at 70.9 million acres, which is the highest since 1982.
Most end-users are believed to be covered at least through the end of the July 4th holiday weekend, so most dealers expect this week to be a slow one.
"Meal users are contnent to watch this market continue to fall," said one Indiana dealer.
Basis offers in Mankato, Minn. were higher Monday in anticipation of local downtime, dealers said.
